tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Diagnose...', 'Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (endpoint fails, errors, slow, cannot be reached) rather than internal implementation, explicitly lists many trigger contexts (health check failures, KMS/S3 artifact issues, VPC reachability, ModelError, multi-model latency, autoscaling, zero-downtime deploys, data capture, monitoring questions) even when the user doesn't name the domain directly, and also explicitly carves out adjacent domains (serverless/async, batch) to sharpen scope. It is a dense but bounded paragraph, appropriate given the breadth of triggers it must cover.
tests.evidence: "Diagnose an Amazon SageMaker real-time inference endpoint that fails, errors, cannot be reached or is slow. Use this skill when creating or updating an endpoint fails or leaves it Failed...even if they do not mention FailureReason, port 8080, VPC endpoints, security groups, data capture or scaling policies by name."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body consistently uses SageMaker-specific, domain-specific procedures (check-ids, API calls, metric namespaces, known traps) rather than explaining general concepts. It assumes the agent already knows what SageMaker/CloudWatch/VPC are and jumps straight into project-specific conventions like the LLM-SM catalog and the two-namespace rule.
tests.evidence: "Grounded in checks-sagemaker-inference-endpoints.md; load it when a symptom matches a row below. Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body keeps the LLM-SM check table as a concise index (one row per check, pointing to the reference for full detail) rather than embedding detection rules, remediations, or citations directly. No large reference blocks are duplicated in the body.
tests.evidence: "The full six-column detection rules, remediations, and citations live in the reference — the table below is a what-it-catches index."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file under references/ is linked via markdown link format in the body at least once.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by clear conditions for when to load it, e.g. tied to specific symptoms, steps, or review stages.
tests.evidence: "load it before interpreting any response that looks clean, empty or InService", "load it at Step 5, when reading the AWS/SageMaker and /aws/sagemaker/Endpoints metric sets"

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at 'references/<filename>' with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (guardrails, review procedure, validation checklist) are given exact prescriptive steps, while flexible areas (how to phrase findings, how to interpret causes) retain reasoning/explanation rather than rigid scripts.
tests.evidence: "Non-negotiable, at every step: 1. Read-only. Never call UpdateEndpoint..." paired with "Each step is best-effort: if an API is denied... record that signal as unavailable and continue"

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present competing tools as equal options; it routes to specific APIs/checks per symptom via the Router table, each symptom having one clear path.
tests.evidence: "| The endpoint isn't scaling, there's no auto-scaling | application-autoscaling:DescribeScalableTargets for the variant | ... |"

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure and Router teach a generalizable approach (symptom matching, step-by-step collection and validation) applicable to any endpoint, not a one-off declaration for a specific instance.
tests.evidence: "Run the steps in order and track progress against this checklist. Each step depends on state gathered by the one before it."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an explicit 'Common wrong answers' section plus 'Error Handling' with named traps (§1-§3) documenting non-obvious pitfalls specific to this domain.
tests.evidence: "'The endpoint is InService, so it's serving traffic.' InService is control-plane state; a variant can be InService with CurrentInstanceCount = 0..."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces health reports and references an explicit template asset for that output.
tests.evidence: "When a full report is requested, the output follows endpoint-health-report-template.md."

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline template exists in the body; the report template is stored in assets/ and only referenced conditionally.
tests.evidence: "load when a full report is requested: endpoint report format (per-endpoint state, findings with check-ids and severities, right-sizing conclusion citing both namespaces, disclosed scope)."

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file is explicitly linked in the body.
tests.evidence: "[endpoint-health-report-template.md](assets/endpoint-health-report-template.md) — load when a full report is requested"

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies exactly when to load it: when a full report is requested.
tests.evidence: "load when a full report is requested: endpoint report format (per-endpoint state, findings with check-ids and severities, right-sizing conclusion citing both namespaces, disclosed scope)."

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure is presented as an ordered checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' format, and the detailed sub-section (Step 5 detail) explicitly references the step number from the checklist.
tests.evidence: "- [ ] Step 1: Enumerate endpoints and resolve their real state." ... "### Step 5 detail: the two-namespace rule"

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation section instructing the agent to re-check its output before presenting, covering check-id accuracy, observed vs inferred values, and disclosed gaps.
tests.evidence: "Before presenting, re-check your output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion."
